chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: Eddie South, and Earl Hines hidden behind a screen
summary: Praises violinist Eddie South; Willard adds Hines' story of being screened from view.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Now, there's a name for you. Eddie South was equipped for symphony, but he was ahead of his time. He had studied abroad and everything. But he played modern jazz as well. So he played better jazz on the violin than any violinist, including Joe Venuti, Stuff Smith, any of the rest of them. Because it was clean, in tune, and he knew what he was doing. The Dark Angel of the South. That's what they called him.
Earl Hines told me that he was in a hotel in Chicago, where he was playing with a white band, they dropped a screen in front of him so that the people that were there to hear him couldn't see him.
Because they couldn't have mixed bands on the bandstand in Chicago.
